answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring each identity to stake a bond locked for a season, like a pearl sealed in a vault: creating thousands of fake agents then costs thousands of bonds, and misbehavior forfeits the stake. Reputation accrues only through verified work over time, so a fresh identity starts on the lowest knoll of trust and must climb by doing real jobs. A zephyr of new accounts may blow in, but without stake and history they cannot vote, price goods, or drain rewards, so attacker cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once.
